paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.

model_annotations.English: This line plot compares the performance of two example selection strategies—ST-ES and Random—as measured by the metric minADE₂₀ (in units of length, likely meters) across varying numbers of in-context examples, ranging from 0 to 8. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Examples,” uses a linear scale with integer tick marks at intervals of 2 (0, 2, 4, 6, 8). The y-axis, labeled “minADE₂₀ (←)”, also uses a linear scale, ranging from approximately 2.60 to 2.85. The ST-ES strategy is represented by a blue line with circular markers and a solid line style; it begins at a value of approximately 2.85 when the number of examples is 0, then sharply declines to a minimum of approximately 2.58 at 2 examples, before gradually increasing to approximately 2.64 at 8 examples. The Random strategy is represented by an orange line with triangular markers and a solid line style; it starts at approximately 2.86, fluctuates slightly above 2.75, and ends at approximately 2.78.
model_annotations.German: The line chart compares the performance of two example selection methods—ST-ES and Random—as measured by minADE₂₀ (in meters) across varying numbers of in-context examples, ranging from 0 to 8, with tick marks at regular intervals of 2. The x-axis is labeled “Number of Examples” and uses a linear scale. The y-axis is labeled “minADE₂₀ (m)” and also uses a linear scale, spanning from approximately 2.60 to 2.85. The ST-ES method is represented by a blue line with circular markers and a solid line style; it begins at approximately 2.85 at 0 examples, sharply decreases to approximately 2.60 at 2 examples, and then remains relatively flat until 6 examples, after which it slightly increases to approximately 2.64 at 8 examples. The Random method is represented by an orange line with circular markers and a solid line style; it starts at approximately 2.86 at 0 examples, decreases to approximately 2.80 at 2 examples, fluctuates between approximately 2.76 and 2.80 for the remaining points, and ends at approximately 2.78 at 8 examples.
